adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Morning...?"
comments: Previous scene is dream/flashback. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The drowsy recognition that morning has arrived is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 身を起こす。
adjudicated.en: I got off the bed,
adjudicated.assessment: 身を起こす means raising one's body or sitting up. 'Got off the bed' carries the action through to leaving the bed, adding a different endpoint not stated by the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I sat up.'

adjudicated.jp: 変哲のない自分の部屋だ。
adjudicated.en: in my room of no unusuality.
comments: Contrast room in the Hasekura Mansion. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The room's complete ordinariness is recoverable despite the unnatural noun 'unusuality.'

adjudicated.jp: うるさく鳴いている時計を止める。
adjudicated.en: I stop the annoying wail of the alarm clock.
comments: Say goodbye to it, for it will never ever be heard again. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Stopping the noisily ringing alarm clock is accurately conveyed through stopping its annoying wail.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "fWah..."
adjudicated.assessment: The sleepy exhalation or yawn is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 夏休みが開けて、９月の頭。
adjudicated.en: It's the beginning of September, as opened by Summer vacation.
comments: A hideously pretentious way of saying "the first week of September was vacation". Although September is the ninth month, http://www.etymonline.com/index.php?term=September etymoloy of the English/Western words for it make it a 7. Translingualism continues. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source places the scene at the start of September after summer vacation has ended. 'Opened by Summer vacation' instead makes the vacation inaugurate the period and reverses the temporal relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Summer vacation was over, and it was the beginning of September.'

adjudicated.jp: 室内には夏の熱気がじわじわと満ちつつある。
adjudicated.en: The Summer heat slowly leaks out from inside the room.
comments: Because Summer is ending, or because of Heat Death of Parallel World - not necessarily because his window is open. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 満ちつつある says the summer heat is gradually filling the room. The English has it leaking out of the room, reversing the direction and changing accumulation into dispersal.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The room was gradually filling with the summer heat.'

highlights.text: leaks out from inside the room

adjudicated.jp: のたくた着替えて、のたくた鞄を手にする。
adjudicated.en: Sluggishly I change into the uniform, sluggishly I take the bag in my hand.
comments: No mention of the Taichi Bag. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His sluggish change of clothes and equally sluggish retrieval of his bag are preserved; specifying a uniform is contextually plausible but added.

adjudicated.jp: 食卓の上に、ラップをかけたサンドイッチが置いてある。
adjudicated.en: On top of the dining table lies a sandwich in a plastic wrap,
adjudicated.assessment: The plastic-wrapped sandwich left on the dining table is accurately retained despite the article error.

adjudicated.jp: 卵と野菜とポテトのサンドだ。
adjudicated.en: a sandwich with eggs, lettuce and potatoes.
comments: Seems like a single one, no paper bags of them, nor lunch, nor a note. Very off-pattern. Of course: it hasn't gotten Fixed yet. Pretty impressive how this being obviously older writing still fits seamlessly into the plot without needing (much of a) fanwank. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The egg and potato fillings are preserved, but 野菜 means vegetables generally. 'Lettuce' selects one specific vegetable without support in the text.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'egg, vegetable, and potato sandwiches' unless the artwork establishes lettuce.

adjudicated.jp: ありがたくいただくことにする。
adjudicated.en: I appropriate it with humble thanks.
adjudicated.assessment: His grateful acceptance and consumption of the food remain recoverable, though 'appropriate' is an unnatural verb.

adjudicated.jp: 「むぐ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Munch."
comments: I'm not certain of the relative legislation, but it might be illegal in some countries to use a SFX for eating other than "nom". If this could cause issues let me know; it's not because I don't want people arrested for owning illegal SFX, just to come laugh at you for being arrested for living in places where possession of certain SFX is a crime. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The muffled eating sound is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: さすが、うまい。
adjudicated.en: Delicious, as typical.
comments: These are intended to be Youko's. Or are they? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The judgment that it is delicious as expected is preserved despite the unidiomatic phrase 'as typical.'

adjudicated.jp: 生活能力皆無な俺にとって、この差し入れはまさに福音。
adjudicated.en: To this me so incapable of managing my own life, this supply drop is the good news.
comments: THE good news, AKA the Gospel. Byble gameZ11! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: For someone unable to manage daily life, the food being a godsend is preserved through the literal 'good news' image.

adjudicated.jp: 通学途中でコンビニ襲撃しないですんだ。
adjudicated.en: I needn't assault a Kombini on the way to school now.
comments: TL Note: if you made it this far without knowing what a Kombini is, ask whoever installed the patch for you. He's probably the guy moving the mouse for you and reading this stuff and explaining to you every word veeery slooowly. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The joke that he no longer needs to raid a convenience store on the way to school is preserved, although the loanword is only romanized.

adjudicated.jp: 「いつもおいしいご飯、ごちそうさまです」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "For food always so delicious, my sincere thanks."
comments: Not what I will use, but since it'd be redundant... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His formal gratitude for the consistently delicious meals is accurately retained despite stiff English.

adjudicated.jp: 東側に手をついて頭を下げる。
adjudicated.en: I bowed my head towards the East, hands hailing towards the ground.
comments: Youko's house. I don't think he literally puts his hands on the ground tho. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His bow toward the east with his hands placed down is recoverable, although 'hands hailing towards the ground' is malformed.

adjudicated.jp: さ、学校だ。
adjudicated.en: So, school.
adjudicated.assessment: The transition to heading for school is retained in a terse fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 上見坂市はその名の通り坂が多い。
adjudicated.en: As the name implies, Kamisaka (Look at the Top of the Hill) has way many hills.
comments: http://www.yado.co.jp/kankou/nagasaki/tushima/kamizakak/kamizakak.htm hmmmmmmmmm, I don't see it. The meaning is closer to "look up at the hill" or "seen from above the hill", but given the whole point of this is a pun between "Hill of God" and a hint that the hokora is important - the hill is the mountain, see CCA0002 - might as well make this more explicit. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The city having many slopes as its name suggests is preserved. The parenthetical English decomposition of the place name is added, awkward, and not securely equivalent to the written name.
adjudicated.remedy: State that Kamisaka has many slopes, just as its name suggests, without forcing an English name gloss.

adjudicated.jp: 学校にたどりつくまで、いくつも斜面を越えていく必要がある。
adjudicated.en: It is necessary to cross a great number of slopes before one at long last reaches school.
adjudicated.assessment: The need to cross numerous slopes before reaching school is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 学校に行くために、上り下り上り下り。
adjudicated.en: Up and down and up and down, just to go to school.
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated up-and-down travel required to reach school is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: それはまるで人生のような波乱を思わせ、往く者の心と足をげんなりとさせるのである。
adjudicated.en: They remind of the storminess that is human life, filling with weariness the hearts and feet of those who travel on ahead.
comments: Because life and going to school and SYMBOLISM!!! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The slopes' evocation of life's turbulence and their exhaustion of travelers' hearts and feet are preserved despite calqued syntax.

adjudicated.jp: 「だる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So heavy..."
adjudicated.assessment: だる is a clipped complaint of sluggishness, weariness, or 'what a drag.' 'So heavy' can suggest physical weight rather than the speaker's fatigue, though the following line partially restores the meaning.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'What a drag...' or 'I'm beat.'

adjudicated.jp: 慣れていてもだるい。
adjudicated.en: I'm used to this, but still I feel sluggish.
adjudicated.assessment: His continuing sluggishness despite being accustomed to the route is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 徒歩はまだいい。
adjudicated.en: Walking is still fine,
adjudicated.assessment: Walking being comparatively tolerable is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 自転車で坂を越えるのは、もっと大変。
adjudicated.en: going around these hills with a bike would be much more of a problem.
comments: This would indicate problems with Nanaka, but look at Sakuraba and, most importantly, Taichi effortlessly chasing Kiri in a bike when she goes for training. See CCZAS: him using a bike even there is symbol for -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The greater difficulty of crossing the slopes by bicycle is broadly present, but 'going around these hills' can mean circumventing them rather than climbing or crossing them.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Getting over these hills by bike would be even harder.'

adjudicated.jp: 自転車はそもそも平地用。
adjudicated.en: Bicycles are conceived for flat ground.
adjudicated.assessment: The point that bicycles are fundamentally intended for flat ground is preserved, though 'conceived' is stilted.

adjudicated.jp: 徒歩より厳しいのぼりと、一瞬で終わる至福のくだり。
adjudicated.en: Climbs harder than a walk, descents that are a fleeting instant of bliss.
comments: The bike or, because there's no point kidding ourselves, SYMBOLISM!!! of how the climbs are still harsh. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The harder-than-walking climbs and momentary bliss of the descents are both accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 苦難の時だけが延々と続いているような気にさせる。
adjudicated.en: That made me feel as if only the times of our hardships would continue on endlessly.
comments: This sounds like it walked out of Isaiah. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The feeling that only hardship continues without end is preserved; 'our' makes the hardship slightly more collective than the unmarked source.

adjudicated.jp: 坂のてっぺんで、商店街に繋がる交差点に合流する。
adjudicated.en: The shopping street that leads from downtown connects into a crossing at the summit of the hill.
comments: See map. Connect, crossing are returning terms because SYMBOLISM but also troll. 'Shopping street' will be used to indicate the Tasaki store area here, at the edge of downtown, but not actual downtown, so I indicate both anyway. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source has the traveler or route join an intersection at the top of the hill, with that intersection leading to the shopping district. The English makes the shopping street itself connect into the crossing and adds an unsupported downtown origin.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'At the top of the hill, I join the intersection leading to the shopping district.'

highlights.text: The shopping street that leads from downtown connects into a crossing

adjudicated.jp: 美希は一年後輩。
adjudicated.en: Miki is my Kouhai, a first year.
adjudicated.assessment: Miki's status as a junior by one school year is conveyed. Leaving 'Kouhai' untranslated is a localization choice rather than a source error.

adjudicated.jp: 世界的に激有名なファンタジー作品に出てくる三人組の、魔法使いの少女みたいな髪型をしている。
adjudicated.en: She has a hairstyle similar to that of those three female magicians in that fantasy series that's super famous worldwide.
comments: Just about every hint point to the TV series Charmed. Of course he can't reference Harry Potter inside his universe, the movie is 2001 and the Japanese translation of the book is 1999. Until he will, of course. Witches return, and most importantly, Cross Channel is closer to fantasy with a sci-fi coat than anything. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The comparison to the hairstyle of a magical-girl trio in a world-famous fantasy work is preserved without supplying a specific title.

adjudicated.jp: ルックスもまあ、似たようなものだ。
adjudicated.en: Looks, certainly, but the resemblance is more thorough.
adjudicated.assessment: The source casually adds that her looks are similar too. 'But the resemblance is more thorough' preserves resemblance but invents a contrast and strengthens its extent.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Her looks are pretty similar too.'

adjudicated.jp: 魔法は使えないが、言葉の魔法使いと呼ばれる。
adjudicated.en: She might not be able to use magic, but one could call her a sorceress of words.
comments: This won't play *that* much, as with much of Week 1 it's a relatively early treatment and things aren't quite settled yet, but indeed taking Miki underhand is a biiig problem here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her inability to use magic and her description as a sorceress of words are preserved; the passive customary label becomes a more hypothetical formulation.

adjudicated.jp: しゃべり出すと止まらないし、しゃべろうとするのを止めることも難しい。
adjudicated.en: It's impossible to stop her once she starts talking, and it's difficult to even stop her from wanting to talk.
adjudicated.assessment: Both her unstoppable speech once started and the difficulty of preventing her from starting are accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 小娘の分際で語彙も豊富なので、話していて飽きない。
adjudicated.en: Her social class is rich in young femaleness, and her vocabulary is similarly rich, so one never grows tired of talking to her.
comments: Sexual implication that she's fun to talk to because she's hot + contrast with her being poor in money (not yet stated). Also they can fight with words and so she's his waifu forever and also ever. Social standing will sort of return. Love how of all OMFG HARD KANJI's here, "vocabulary" is furry'd. The reason is that 彙 wasn't joyo until 2010, so there's nothing deep about it, but it's funny in retrospect. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 小娘の分際で is a disparaging concessive, roughly 'for a little girl like her,' not a statement that her social class is rich in femininity. The English replaces the contrast between youth and vocabulary with a nonsensical social classification.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'For a little girl, she has a rich vocabulary, so talking to her never gets boring.'

highlights.text: Her social class is rich in young femaleness

adjudicated.jp: 美希はもう一人の一年生部員・佐倉霧とよくつるんでいる。
adjudicated.en: Miki is often found mate-ing with one other first year member of the club, the one with the Japanese word for fog for a name, Sakura Kiri.
comments: "Mate-ing" will recur, plus vague lesbian subtext. There's several fog puns 'round her route especially, so here's your warning. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: つるんでいる says that Miki often hangs out or associates with Kiri. 'Mate-ing' adds an animal or sexual implication, while the explanatory gloss of Kiri's name is absent from the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Miki often hangs out with the club's other first-year member, Sakura Kiri.'

highlights.text: the one with the Japanese word for fog for a name,

adjudicated.jp: ロングヘアの美希と、中性的な容姿でショートヘアの霧。
adjudicated.en: Miki the long haired one, and Kiri the androgynous short-haired one:
adjudicated.assessment: Miki's long hair and Kiri's androgynous appearance and short hair are all preserved; the colon simply links the fragment to the next sentence.

adjudicated.jp: 二人揃うと花畑のように場に映える。
adjudicated.en: the two assembled beautify the place like a flower bed.
adjudicated.assessment: The image of the pair brightening the setting like a flower bed is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 部のマスコット的な存在だ。
adjudicated.en: They are mascot-like presences in our club.
adjudicated.assessment: Their mascot-like place in the club is retained, though 'presences' is a literal and awkward choice.

adjudicated.jp: 美希はとにかくミニスカートが大好きだ。いつもはいている。
adjudicated.en: Miki, by the by, really loves miniskirts. She's always in one.
comments: She's never OUT of one outside of sex scenes, though it's not like the dress code of Gunjou is that impressive (forget Touko, are Kiri and Misato going to the same school?) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Miki's love of miniskirts and habit of always wearing one are accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: しかも素直で可愛い。ノリもいい。
adjudicated.en: And she's so upfront and adorable. We mash together well.
comments: "We get along well" + "Riding her is fine too." -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her frank, lovable nature and easy rapport are recoverable. 'Mash together' is distinctly unnatural but still communicates compatibility.

adjudicated.jp: 俺もミニスカート大好きなことを差し引いても、気が合わない理由がない。
adjudicated.en: Even setting aside how I also really love miniskirts, there's no reason for us not to get along.
comments: Given his backstory this has multiple meanings, that "even", in particular. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The aside about his own love of miniskirts and the conclusion that they have every reason to get along are both preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 卒業するとき、制服をもらう約束も取りつけてある。
adjudicated.en: When she graduates, I had her promise to give me her uniform.
adjudicated.assessment: The secured promise that he will receive her uniform upon graduation is preserved despite a slightly loose tense choice.

adjudicated.jp: かわりに第二ボタンをあげようという提案は、丁重に断られてしまったけど。
adjudicated.en: However, the proposal to give her the second button of my uniform in return was courteously and thoroughly declined.
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_school_uniform wow it's on Wikipedia, too. She's just teasing him anyway. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His proposed exchange of his second uniform button and her polite refusal are accurate; 'thoroughly' modestly intensifies 丁重に.

adjudicated.jp: 「ちわーす」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "G'mooorn."
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out, casual greeting is represented functionally in the morning context.

adjudicated.jp: 商店街のはしっこにある店に入る。
adjudicated.en: I entered the shop at the very edge of the shopping street:
adjudicated.assessment: Entering the shop at the edge of the shopping street is accurately conveyed; the colon prepares the displayed shop name.

adjudicated.jp: 『田崎食料』
adjudicated.en: 『Tasaki Groceries』
adjudicated.assessment: The shop name is translated directly and consistently.

adjudicated.jp: 「もしもーし」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Anyone heeere?"
adjudicated.assessment: The elongated call asking whether anyone is present is represented naturally.

adjudicated.jp: 奥に声をかける。
adjudicated.en: I call towards the back of the store.
adjudicated.assessment: Calling toward the back of the shop is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 反応はない。
adjudicated.en: There's no response.
adjudicated.assessment: The lack of a response is conveyed exactly; present tense is a narrative-style choice.

adjudicated.jp: 「……不在か」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...unmanned?"
adjudicated.assessment: The conclusion that nobody is present is retained, though 'unmanned' is unusually mechanical for the thought.

adjudicated.jp: 田崎食料はここしばらく、不在続きだ。
adjudicated.en: Tasaki Groceries had been often left unmanned of late.
comments: That's sooo convenient, isn't it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The shop's repeated recent lack of an attendant is preserved despite awkward English syntax.

adjudicated.jp: ここの店主、田崎吾一郎氏（４７歳・独身）は無類の鉄道マニアだ。
adjudicated.en: The shopkeeper here, a Tasaki Goichirou (age 47, single) is an unrivaled railway enthusiast.
comments: technically it *is* Mr. Tasaki, but that sounds just so damn off with the honorifics. Reality's unrealistic and all that. He's single because he's a Priest of God... no, I seriously suspect he is, just like Taichi will end up eternally single given he's lost in his own world. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The shopkeeper's name, age, marital status, and exceptional enthusiasm for railways are all retained; the indefinite article before his name is awkward.

adjudicated.jp: よくふらりと店をあけ、遠方の土地にローカル線の写真を撮りに行く。
adjudicated.en: He must've casually opened the store, then trundled off to some faraway place to take pictures of their local train line.
adjudicated.assessment: In context 店をあけ means leaving or vacating the shop while wandering off, not opening it for business. The English reverses that action before correctly describing the trip to photograph a distant local railway.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'He often wanders away from the shop to photograph local railway lines in far-off places.'

adjudicated.jp: で、その間も店をあけているのである。
adjudicated.en: And, all the while, the shop still stays open.
adjudicated.assessment: The fact that the shop remains open during the owner's absence is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: つまり無人商店だ。
adjudicated.en: In other words it's a clerk-less store.
adjudicated.assessment: The conclusion that it is an unattended shop is preserved; 'clerk-less' is unconventional but intelligible.

adjudicated.jp: もともと道楽なのだろう。
adjudicated.en: This shop had likely been an amusement for him from the beginning.
adjudicated.assessment: The inference that the shop was a hobby or indulgence from the outset is retained through 'amusement.'

adjudicated.jp: ３０代の頃は泣く子を殺すと言われるほどに悪顔だった氏だが、ご両親の死後しばらくを経て、険の取れた豊かな顔つきへと変わっていった。
adjudicated.en: When he was in his thirties, he had the kind of nastiness in his face that is often used to scare crybabies to sleep ("kids who sleep grow up well, kids who cry die"), but sometime after the death of his parents, his face changed into one of abundance, its harshness lost.
comments: I worked in the referenced proverb because Bible Game'ses are only about edutainment, sort of how you learned the totally correct furrygana's up there and how your about to learn how to correctly use 'your' in a sentence. There's another 豊, hope that's clear enough that this is a reference to a major subtext in CC. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source hyperbolically says his face was so villainous that people said it could kill a crying child. The English changes killing into frightening children to sleep and inserts an unrelated explanatory proverb, materially rewriting the image.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'In his thirties, he looked so menacing people said his face could kill a crying child.'

highlights.text: he had the kind of nastiness in his face that is often used to scare crybabies to sleep ("kids who sleep grow up well, kids who cry die")

adjudicated.jp: 遺産以外の何が、元暴走族の粗暴な鉄オタを善人に変えうるというのか。
adjudicated.en: Something outside the inheritance has changed someone who's more of a member of a biker gang than a railway fanatic into a nice guy, perhaps.
comments: See CCX0001. This guy's the Greek chorus: what happened to him is religious conversion. I suspect the hospital, too. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source asks rhetorically what other than an inheritance could have turned a rough former biker-gang member and railway obsessive into a good person. The English instead asserts that something outside the inheritance did so, loses 'former,' and converts two traits into a comparison between them.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'What besides an inheritance could turn a rough former biker and train fanatic into a good man?'

highlights.text: Something outside the inheritance has changed someone who's more of a member of a biker gang than a railway fanatic into a nice guy, perhaps.

adjudicated.jp: 持ち歩いているメモ帳に、ペンを走らせる。
adjudicated.en: I run the pen on the notebook I carry around.
comments: Oddly, it seems the actual memos aren't provided by the shop. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Writing in the notebook he carries is preserved, though 'run the pen on' is a close Japanese-shaped calque.

adjudicated.jp: 『９／７、緑茶王、１３０円……黒須太一』
adjudicated.en:
9/7
Green King Tea
130￥
Kurosu Taichi
comments: HACK massive reformatting for slightly above average justice. This may be relevant, may be not: http://dic.nicovideo.jp/a/%E7%B7%91%E8%8C%B6%E7%8E%8B -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 緑茶王 is the compound 'Green Tea King.' 'Green King Tea' changes which words form the product name and no longer represents the source's title-like 王 construction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Green Tea King.'

adjudicated.jp: 備え付けのテープで、壁にぺたりと貼りつける。
adjudicated.en: With the adhesive tape provided, I stick the note to the wall.
comments: ...but the tape is? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Using the supplied tape to stick the note flat against the wall is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 見ると、もう何枚ものメモが張ってある。
adjudicated.en: Looking closer, there are several of these memos are up already.
adjudicated.assessment: Several notes already being posted is accurately conveyed despite the duplicated verb in 'there are ... are up.'

adjudicated.jp: 「あ、美希のやつ、もう行っちゃったのか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ah, that Miki, did she already go on ahead?"
adjudicated.assessment: The casual realization that Miki has already left or gone ahead is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 『９／３、野菜ジュース健々ＧＯＧＯ、１１０円……山辺美希』
adjudicated.en:
9/3
Vegetable Juice Health Pandemonium
110￥
Yamanobe Miki
comments: Lit. healthy-healthy Gogo, but it's pronounced as 喧々囂々 kenkengogo tumult/clamor/pandemonium. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The date, vegetable drink, price, and purchaser are accurate. 'Health Pandemonium' attempts to preserve the product's sound-based wordplay rather than translating it literally.

adjudicated.jp: 『９／３、マグナムライチ、１１０円……桜庭浩』『ピリッと辛いです』
adjudicated.en:
9/3
Magnum Lychee
110￥
Sakuraba Hiroshi
Pungently peppery
comments: Original term googles, but no idea what the equivalent would be. Connotation of comment seems ambiguous. True Mr. Exposition leaving comments to the Greek Chorus is just one of the many tiny little details that make Cross Channel as good as it is. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The product, price, purchaser, and comment that it has a sharp spicy kick are all retained.

adjudicated.jp: 『９／４、ペットボトル天然水、１４０円……宮澄見里』
adjudicated.en:
9/4
Bottle of Natural Water
140￥
Miyasumi Misato

adjudicated.en: When it's time for the bill, there'll be hell to pay here.
comments: Total 440 yen 4+4+0=8. Indeed, once the bill comes that'll be a problem since things simply don't add up to 8. And, of course, this pointing out - like the clock thing in her route - is there to hint that she's lying about something, in this case what she buys. -GHS

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭、感想いらない。

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hm?"
adjudicated.assessment: The brief questioning reaction is represented directly.

adjudicated.jp: そのアホの桜庭の裏にもう一枚張ってある。
adjudicated.en: Behind Sakuraba's idiocies, there's one more sheet.
comments: THE TRUTH WAS BEHIND SAKURABA ALL ALONG, AND TOUKO KNOWS IT. Or something. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source locates another sheet behind the one belonging to 'that idiot Sakuraba.' 'Behind Sakuraba's idiocies' turns the concrete note and insulting description into an abstract plurality of foolish acts, though the physical relation remains inferable.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'There was another sheet posted behind that idiot Sakuraba's.'

adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Milady, getting greedy and taking three whole bottles!'

adjudicated.jp: お金持ちなのに恥ーずかしい、あーさましいー。
adjudicated.en: You're so rich, but this is embaraaassing, and shaaamefuuul!
comments: Although in retrospect, this is actually a DOUBLE SYMBOLISM!!! as in, her wanting to subsist on water alone is sort of like wanting to subsist on Taichi's dick (certainly not his love) alone. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out teasing that such behavior is embarrassing and shameful despite wealth is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 一番目立つところに張り直してやる。
adjudicated.en: I'll put it back in the most prominent spot.
adjudicated.assessment: Reposting the note in the most conspicuous location is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: ぺたりこ
adjudicated.en: Stick!
adjudicated.assessment: The playful sound or mimetic expression of sticking the note down is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 「これでよし、と」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And with this, we're good."
adjudicated.assessment: The satisfied conclusion that the adjustment will do is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 店の奥に行って、緑茶のボトルを一本取ってくる。
adjudicated.en: I went into the back of the store and grabbed one bottle of tea.
adjudicated.assessment: Going to the back and taking a bottle is preserved, but 緑茶 specifically identifies green tea while the English reduces it to generic tea.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I went to the back of the shop and grabbed a bottle of green tea.'

adjudicated.jp: 「じゃ、ツケということで」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well then, let's say that's on credit."
comments: Subtle hint that there'll be no one to actually call on it? Of course there's technically no problem. Tasaki's technically loaded so he wouldn't care too much, whether one interprets the concepts of forgiveness of debts in this literal sense or not. Or whether the debt these people are in with Tasaki is literal or not. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The casual declaration that the purchase will go on the tab is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 店を出た。
adjudicated.en: I left the store.
adjudicated.assessment: Leaving the shop is conveyed exactly.

adjudicated.jp: 緑茶を喉に流し込みながら、学校に向かった。
adjudicated.en: Pouring tea down my throat, I headed towards school.
comments: Him going to the shop anyway contradicts the beginning except for this detail: the difference between Youko and Mutsumi seems to be that the latter doesn't forget drinks, see CCA0013. Then again, drinks never come up again as the pattern becomes fixed enough that he just carries a canteen around. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Heading to school while pouring the drink down his throat is preserved. Green tea is generalized to tea, but the immediately preceding purchase keeps the referent recoverable.

adjudicated.jp: 「おやま」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Oh my."
comments: PCP above
adjudicated.assessment: The playful mild surprise is represented directly.

adjudicated.jp: 教室には先客がいた。
adjudicated.en: There was a previous visitor in the classroom.
adjudicated.assessment: 先客 is someone already present who arrived first. 'A previous visitor' can instead suggest a person who visited earlier and has since left, weakening the immediate presence established by the source and following sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Someone had beaten me to the classroom.'

adjudicated.jp: 窓際の席。
adjudicated.en: In a seat in the row next to the window,
comments: Where protagonists usually sit. Not Taichi. This irrelevant detail is, of course, of tremendous significance. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The window-side seat is preserved as a fragment leading into the next description.

adjudicated.jp: 立て肘をついて座っている少女が、ちらと一瞥をよこす。
adjudicated.en: there sat a girl, with her elbow on the table, sends a single peeking glance my way.
comments: Some of these older descriptions don't quite match the CGs. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The seated girl, propped elbow, and brief glance are all preserved. The English is grammatically tangled and specifies a table or desk not named in the source.

adjudicated.en: Touko: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent response is represented directly; the canonical occurrence is uniquely bracketed by the resolved neighboring units.

adjudicated.jp: 言葉はなく、視線を外に戻した。
adjudicated.en: Without a word, she returns her line of sight to the outside.
adjudicated.assessment: Silently returning her gaze outside is preserved; 'line of sight' is an overly technical calque.

adjudicated.jp: 「お早いご通学で」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You're quick on your school commute."
comments: Her house is technically closer than Taichi's. Joking formality that could easily be read as scornful. The possibility she spends day and night at school is far from remote, given how it's possibly around 1AM. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: お早い comments with mock politeness on her being at school early. 'Quick on your school commute' instead describes speed or efficiency during the journey and misses the early-arrival point.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'You're at school early.' with an appropriately teasing formal tone.

adjudicated.en: Touko: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The continued silence is represented directly; the canonical occurrence is uniquely bracketed by the resolved neighboring units.

adjudicated.jp: 「しかもまた私服通学か」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And yet you came to school in normal clothes again?"
adjudicated.assessment: The remark that she has again come to school in ordinary clothes rather than a uniform is preserved; 'normal clothes' is slightly imprecise but clear.

adjudicated.jp: 「よくそんな暑そうな格好ができるな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You really manage to wear that hot-looking thing often, can't you."
comments: Since she's always in that dress, and how she has multiple of them at home will become a joke later on, emphasis on 'often'. I actually wonder if that "hot" is meant English style as well. Taichi may not know English, but that doesn't stop him from affecting himself American or at least non-Japanese, especially 'round this first route. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Here よく expresses amazement at how she can bear such warm-looking clothing, not frequency. The English inserts 'often' and leaves 'hot-looking' open to a different sense instead of describing an outfit that looks stifling.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'How can you stand wearing something that looks so hot?'

adjudicated.en: Touko: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated silent response is represented directly; the canonical occurrence is uniquely bracketed by the resolved neighboring units.

adjudicated.jp: 無視。
adjudicated.en: Ignored.
adjudicated.assessment: The terse statement that he is ignored is preserved in fragmentary form.

adjudicated.jp: 「へいへい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hey hey."
adjudicated.assessment: へいへい is a resigned or dismissive 'yeah, yeah' or 'all right, all right.' Rendering it as the attention-getting greeting 'hey hey' changes the speech act.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Yeah, yeah.'

adjudicated.jp: 肩をすくめて、冬子のすぐ隣……自分の席に座る。
adjudicated.en: Shrugging my shoulder, I sit in the seat next Touko's... mine.
comments: Possibly actually his, possibly irrelevant because there's no classes/this is Youko's Special Classroom/Class X. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Shrugging and sitting in his own seat immediately beside Touko are preserved despite singular 'shoulder' and a missing preposition.

adjudicated.jp: まるでハリネズミだ。
adjudicated.en: Just like a hedgehog.
comments: The only direct reference to the fairly trite Hedgehog Dilemma throughout the story, mercifully. The needles could actually be HIS, however. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The hedgehog comparison is translated directly.

adjudicated.jp: 最近は、針に磨きがかかっている。
adjudicated.en: And lately, taken to polishing those needles.
adjudicated.assessment: 針に磨きがかかっている says the figurative quills have lately become even sharper or more formidable. The English invents an omitted subject actively taking up the habit of polishing them.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Lately, her quills have grown sharper still.'

adjudicated.jp: 誰に対してもそうだから、気に病むこともない。
adjudicated.en: It's the same with everyone, so it's nothing to be worried about.
adjudicated.assessment: The reassurance that she behaves that way toward everyone and therefore need not cause worry is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: けど俺に対しての針は……少し毒を含んでいる気がする。
adjudicated.en: But the needles set against me... feel like they have a bit of poison in them.
comments: This could still be him: the fight with himself is spiritual, after all. See CCZAS: delayed poison attack as what uhmmm let's say SYMBOLISM and move on. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The impression that the figurative quills directed at him contain a little poison is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 気のせいかもしれない。
adjudicated.en: Maybe it's just my imagination, I don't know,
adjudicated.assessment: The possibility that it is only his imagination is preserved; 'I don't know' adds conversational hesitation.

adjudicated.jp: 自意識過剰なだけかも。
adjudicated.en: it might just be my excessive self-consciousness, perhaps,
comments: Body Dismorphic Disorder awareness? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His thought that he may simply be overly self-conscious is retained, though the nominal phrasing is stiff.

adjudicated.jp: けど。
adjudicated.en: but,
adjudicated.assessment: The isolated adversative fragment is retained as part of the accumulating hesitation.

adjudicated.jp: けれども。
adjudicated.en: and also however,
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated adversative hesitation is preserved, although 'and also however' is deliberately cumbersome English.

adjudicated.jp: そう考えただけで。
adjudicated.en: just by thinking that,
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment stating that merely thinking it was enough is preserved as part of the accumulating sentence.

adjudicated.jp: 発作は起こった。
adjudicated.en: I had a seizure.
comments: See CCA0016/17A. This will not actually return often: Taichi's odd behavior is only really highlighted around this route. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The occurrence of an attack or seizure is directly conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「いかんね。いかんいかん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Cut it out now! Cut it out cut it out!"
adjudicated.assessment: The urgent self-directed rejection that this will not do is represented functionally as an order to stop; 'now' adds intensity.

adjudicated.jp: 幸い発作は小さなもので、理性が消し飛ぶ危険はなかった。
adjudicated.en: Fortunately the fit was small, so there was no danger of it scattering my rationality.
adjudicated.assessment: The attack's limited scale and the absence of danger that reason would be blown away are preserved, though 'scattering my rationality' is an awkward calque.

adjudicated.jp: 逆流した胃液を呑み込む悪寒と引き替えに、そいつの頭を奈落に押し込める。
adjudicated.en: In exchange for the chills of swallowing acid reflux, its head is imprisoned back in the hellish abyss.
comments: Vomit is exactly what Yusa does. Similarly Touko. This is strong evidence that it's Taichi who rejected her, not viceversa. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The physical revulsion, swallowed reflux, and forcing the entity back into an abyss are recoverable. The source makes the narrator actively push its head down; the English changes this to an unexplained passive imprisonment.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'At the cost of shuddering as I swallowed the acid rising in my throat, I shoved its head back into the abyss.'

adjudicated.jp: 異形の舌先が、ちろりと地表を薙いだ。
adjudicated.en: The tip of its heteromorphic tongue is scythed down in a flash, and lays calm on the surface of the earth.
comments: Oddly, that 'scythe down' seems to also mean that, which is the only thing that seems to make sense. Used both as this returns in a highly metaphorical scene in CCD4002. "Chirori" is an illegal and evil SFX as there'll be lots in this accursed moege and they're the #1 reason why Cross Channel is so damn hard to translate. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source makes the tip of the grotesque tongue briefly flick or sweep across the surface. The English instead makes the tongue the passive object of being scythed down and adds that it comes to rest calmly, reversing agency and inventing a result.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'The tip of its misshapen tongue flicked across the surface.'

highlights.text: The tip of its heteromorphic tongue is scythed down in a flash, and lays calm on the surface of the earth.

adjudicated.jp: 「なあ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hey."
adjudicated.assessment: The casual bid for attention is represented naturally.

adjudicated.en: Touko: "...what."
adjudicated.assessment: The terse, reluctant 'what' is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: いい加減うんざりといった調子で、冬子。
adjudicated.en: A tone that sounds just about fed up with fooling around, Touko's.
adjudicated.assessment: Touko's thoroughly fed-up tone is preserved, but 'with fooling around' supplies a specific cause not stated here, and the possessive fragment is malformed.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Touko sounded thoroughly fed up.'

adjudicated.jp: 「お尻のとこ、破れてパンツ見えてる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Around your ass there's a tear, and I can see your panties."
adjudicated.assessment: The crude warning about a tear around the seat exposing her underwear is accurately conveyed.

comments: She takes THIS seriously of him? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The wordless shocked reaction and repeated emphatic punctuation are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 慌てて立ち上がり、両手で尻をまさぐる。
adjudicated.en: Standing up in a panic, she gropes her behind with both hands.
adjudicated.assessment: Standing in panic and feeling around her backside with both hands are accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「なんつったりして」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Awww what a dumb thing I said."
comments: Giko neko/2chan meme. Seems to date to 1999, however, and can't date the meme to 2003 or earlier either. The meme seems to have overtaken all other references. No 'official' English translation that I found, but a literal works anyway. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: なんつったりして is a playful retraction equivalent to 'just kidding' or 'or so I say.' The English turns it into remorseful self-criticism and fails to reveal the preceding claim as a prank.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Just kidding.'

highlights.text: Awww what a dumb thing I said.

adjudicated.jp: ばちーん！！
adjudicated.en: Ker-smack!!!
comments: It's not ANIMU without ker-something. -GHS
SEF 101 0
HACK independent BG shake -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The loud impact sound is represented with a functional English comic-book effect.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぐふっ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "G'fuh!"
adjudicated.assessment: The impact grunt is transliterated functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 不意の平手うち。
adjudicated.en: Sudden palm strike.
adjudicated.assessment: The sudden open-handed blow is preserved; 'palm strike' sounds more technical than the source's slap.

adjudicated.jp: スリップダウン。
adjudicated.en: Bail into slipdown.
comments: Lit. sliding as one bails off a racing motorbike. That one doesn't seem to have a single English term tho. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source consists only of the stylized loan expression 'slip down.' Adding 'bail into' imports an unsupported racing or motorcycle maneuver rather than simply describing the fall.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Slip down.' or a functional 'Down I went.'

adjudicated.jp: 見事に転ぶ。
adjudicated.en: A magnificent fall.
adjudicated.assessment: The spectacular or thorough fall is accurately preserved as a fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 「いててて」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "OwChChCh!"
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated cry of pain is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子はもう、先刻と変わらぬ姿勢で座っていた。
adjudicated.en: Touko was already sitting in the exact unchanging posture as moments before.
adjudicated.assessment: Touko already being seated in precisely the same posture as moments earlier is preserved despite awkward modifiers.

adjudicated.jp: 「冗談だってのに」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But I was just kidding!"
adjudicated.assessment: The protest that it was only a joke is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.en: Touko: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent response is represented directly; the canonical occurrence is uniquely bracketed by the resolved neighboring units.

adjudicated.jp: 相手をしてくれるつもりはないらしい。
adjudicated.en: It doesn't look like she's looking to play around with someone.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says she apparently has no intention of engaging with or humoring him. 'Play around with someone' generalizes the object and adds a playful or sexual implication not required by 相手をする.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Apparently she had no intention of humoring me.'

adjudicated.jp: 澄ましていて排他的で。
adjudicated.en: Clannishly demure.
adjudicated.assessment: Her composed aloofness and exclusionary manner are compressed into an unusual but broadly recoverable phrase.

adjudicated.jp: でも意外と、心の隙は多い。
adjudicated.en: But hearts, surprisingly, have many openings.
adjudicated.assessment: The source remains about this particular person: despite her aloofness, she has surprisingly many openings in her emotional guard. The plural 'hearts' turns the observation into a generic claim and removes its subject.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'But surprisingly, she leaves plenty of openings in her guard.'

adjudicated.jp: 鞄を机に放って、冬子以外誰もいない教室を眺め渡す。
adjudicated.en: I dump my bag on the desk and pass a lost gaze on the classroom, empty with the exception of Touko.
comments: So he had it in his hands when he was punched down? Hints that he never was, perhaps. The Taichi Bag's never described as a backpack, for that matter. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Throwing the bag onto the desk and looking across a classroom empty except for Touko are preserved; 'pass a lost gaze on' is unnatural.

adjudicated.jp: まだ始業まで間がある。
adjudicated.en: There's still time before we begin.
comments: Ambiguous as to what. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The available interval is retained, but 始業 specifically means the start of classes or work. 'Before we begin' supplies an unspecified collective subject and loses the school-time reference.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'There was still time before classes began.'

adjudicated.jp: どうしよう。
adjudicated.en: What to do.
adjudicated.assessment: The brief indecision about what to do is preserved.

withheld.en: I look up at the sky.

withheld.jp: 今日も暑くなるのだろうか。
だが不思議と空気は乾いていて、過ごしやすそうな気配だ。
withheld.en: Yet the air is inexplicably dry, and there's signs it will be pleasantly nice.

withheld.jp: 海から流れてくれ湿気と熱気も、今日は穏やかなのだろうか。
withheld.en: The moisture and the heat that flow in from the sea, as well, should be quite mild today.
comments: However I look these three seem sort of contradictory. Possibly intentional; this route needs a little less actual overwriting and a little more self-parodying. -GHS

withheld.jp: その先には団地があって、ＦＬＯＷＥＲＳの片割れ、山辺美希が住んでいる。
withheld.en: Ahead in that direction is the apartment complex where Yamanobe Miki, one half of the Flowers, lives.
comments: Wow, that's the correct way of writing it! Of course, it's actually a typo, it was fixed to FLOWER'S in the console version. And yes, I am so so so so tempted of doing the same, as I strongly suspect this is more hints of Taichi's ill manners and that readers are supposed to take most of this erudition with a grain or seven of salt. Also keep in mind that he'll later be uncertain as to where Miki lives, whoops. -GHS

withheld.jp: だからＦＬＯＷＥＲＳ（お花ちゃんたち）。
comments: You'll notice the Japanese translation in parenthesis, because furrygana does not technically work the way I use it, but you can't expect furries to teach you about Japanese, can you. -GHS

withheld.jp: もツケてくれる希有な地元密着型店舗なのである。
withheld.en: Anyway, right now the shop owned by this man with a smiling face is one of those very rare, local-contact type stores that allows an unlimited tab for those who live around it.
comments: It's such a convenient coincidence that if the owner wasn't a man of God, and therefore all of this generated by God himself as Providence, and therefore its convenience being itself a major plot point, it'd be bad writing. -GHS
